title: DevEx docs playbook: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, ops, and top support issues
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues + fixes. It is intended to ensure consistent, high-quality, reproducible docs that reduce time-to-value for customers and cut support load for the DevEx team.

Goals:
- Ship clear SDK guides and quickstarts that let engineers integrate Redwood Inference in under 15 minutes.
- Provide canonical API examples for the core product surfaces (text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking).
- Maintain an ops playbook for the docs site (publishing, validation, rollback).
- Maintain a prioritized list of top support issues with reproducible steps and canonical fixes.

Audience:
- SDK authors, technical writers, DevEx engineers, solutions engineers, and on-call support.

Ownership & contacts:
- Primary owner: DevEx docs team (engineering).
- Escalation: Support triage -> DevEx on-call -> Eng runtime team.
- Slack channel: #devex-docs.
- Pager: DevEx on-call rota (see related_pages).

Standards & doc structure (required for every quickstart/SDK guide):
1) Title and short description (1-2 lines).
2) Audience and prerequisites (OS, SDK version, API key scope).
3) Quickstart (single-file working example: copy-paste runnable).
4) API reference links and output shape examples.
5) Troubleshooting and top-of-page support pointers.
6) Tags/labels and last updated date.

Recommended length and style:
- Quickstarts: 2-6 screens (short).
- SDK guides: 800-2000 words with code examples and a small integration walkthrough.
- Tone: concise, example-first, command-line and copyable code blocks.

Quickstart template (example):
---
Title: SDK Quickstart: Text generation with Redwood Python SDK
Description: Minimal example to authenticate and request a streaming completion in Python.
Prereqs:
- Python 3.10+
- pip install redwood-inference==1.4.0
- REDWOOD_API_KEY in env

Copy-paste example (Python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-1.5", prompt="Summarize the following email:\n\nDear team,...")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstart checklist (before publish):
- [ ] Code runs locally with pinned SDK version.
- [ ] Includes expected output example.
- [ ] Minimal reproduction for one common error (auth, version mismatch).
- [ ] Labels: sdk, quickstart, python/js.

API examples (canonical):
Provide a short set of examples for each product surface. Each example must include: request json, expected response snippet, typical param values, and a security note about PII.
- Text generation: sync + streaming + structured output.
- Chat: system + user message handling and function/tool calling example.
- Embeddings: batch upload, vector dimensions, normalization guidance.
- Reranking: sample candidate format and scoring.

Canonical API example (JavaScript streaming):
```javascript
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1.0', messages: [{role: 'system', content: 'You are an assistant.'}, {role: 'user', content: 'Explain prefix caching.'}] })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing flow):
1) Author creates PR against docs repo with markdown/JSON content and preview config.
2) CI runs: spellcheck, link-check, code-sample lint, snippet runnable checks (where applicable).
3) Reviewer (DevEx assigned) approves; label `docs/ready` added.
4) Merge triggers staging deploy and a preview URL in Slack.
5) Smoke test: open quickstart, run the example against a sandbox key.
6) On success, merge staging -> main for production deploy.
7) Any rollback is a revert PR; emergency rollback: trigger `docs-site/rollback` workflow and notify #devex-docs.

Required CI checks:
- link-check (no broken internal links)
- code-snippet lint (formats and language tags)
- runtime smoke (Python/JS quickstarts: run in short-lived containers)

Review checklist for reviewers:
- Accuracy of API parameters and version pins.
- Security: no customer data, no hard-coded secrets, and correct KMS references for private deployment guides.
- Accessibility: headings, alt text for images, and descriptive link text.

Versioning and deprecation policy:
- SDK guides must include SDK version used and the next scheduled review (6 months).
- Mark deprecated samples with `DEPRECATED` and link to migration guide.

Top support issues (canonical list - update monthly):
Table: Issue | Symptom | Replication steps | Canonical fix | Owner
| Authentication failures | 401 API errors from SDK | 1) Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY set 2) Confirm key scope 3) Check clock skew on server | Rotate key, verify permissions; ensure system clock in sync (NTP) | DevEx on-call
| Model mismatch / versioning | Unexpected hallucination or API schema changes | Use pinned model and SDK version; reproduce with minimal prompt | Pin model+SDK; open ADR if model behavior changed | Eng serving-runtime
| Streaming truncated responses | Partial responses + connection closed | Reproduce with long prompt and low timeout | Increase client timeout and enable streaming-reconnect; file bug if runtime closed the stream | Eng runtime/DevEx
| High latency on embeddings | Large batch latencies > target (200ms per request) | Run batch of 100 docs | Batch smaller, enable async batching suggestions; scale Dedicated pool for embeddings | Eng-sre/Platform
| Incorrect JSON output from structured generation | JSON parsing errors in client apps | Reproduce with sample prompt that requests JSON | Add `json_schema` param (SDK) and use structured output validator; add example to quickstart | DevEx + Applied ML

Canonical fixes must include: minimal repro, one-line fix, linked remediation PR or KB article. Each issue entry requires an owner and a runbook link in related_pages.

On-call & escalation (short):
- Triage owner: DevEx support engineer (first 15 minutes)
- If the issue is reproducible and >= Sev2, escalate to Eng runtime or Eng-sre depending on type.
- For customer-impacting regressions, follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.

Metrics & observability for docs impact:
- Track playground runs, quickstart copy clicks, and code snippet run rates.
- Support metrics: number of support tickets linked to docs, time-to-first-response, and mean time to resolution (MTTR) for doc-related cases.

Way of working (templates & PR norms):
- Use the quickstart template in the repo (docs/templates/quickstart.md).
- Keep examples minimal and rely on linked `full-example` repositories for longer integrations.
- Use `labels` and `category` frontmatter for search.
- When shipping a breaking change to SDKs or API: open a docs-announce PR at least 2 weeks before, add migration guide, and schedule a town hall for major customers.

Appendix: Useful snippets and links
- CI command to run snippet smoke tests: `make docs-smoke`
- Local preview: `npm run docs:dev` or `make docs-preview`
- Sandbox API key: request via #devex-sandbox with reason and owner (30-day expiry).

Change log:
- 2026-03-20: Initial draft by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-04-10: Published: added top support issues table and CI requirements (reviewers: Michael Chen, Ravi Kapoor).

If you are updating this playbook: follow the Review checklist and add your name to reviewers. For urgent fixes, open a KB article and ping #devex-docs.
